implementation_notes: Rails' first-party instrumentation API is the bus: ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument('order.placed', order_id: id) publishes a named event with an arbitrary payload hash, subscribe('order.placed') { |event| } registers a handler, and subscriptions may match an exact name, a Regexp, or everything; subscribe returns a subscriber object that unsubscribe takes back, and subscribed scopes a subscription to a block. The event name is a dot-separated string (the event.library convention) and the payload hash is the event data, so the classic event class is unnecessary; for typed domain-event handlers on plain Ruby objects, dry-events or Wisper provide the same structure.
code_sketch:
ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument('order.placed', order_id: order.id)

ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('order.placed') do |event|
  payload = event.payload          # { order_id: 42 }
  Stock.reserve(payload[:order_id])
end
pitfalls: Subscriptions are process-global and never collected: a subscriber registered per request or per object leaks and keeps firing for other tenants unless the returned subscriber object is unsubscribed.
An exception inside an instrumented block still publishes the event, with the exception recorded in the payload, so a subscriber must not assume the operation succeeded.
